paper.title: Algorithm 779: Fermi-Dirac Functions of Order -1/2, 1/2, 3/2, 5/2
paper.venue: ACM Transactions on Mathematical Software 24(1), 1-12 (CALGO Algorithm 779)
paper.url: https://netlib.org/toms/779.gz (ACM article not read: the DL returns 403 to automated fetch)

code.commit: netlib TOMS archive 779.gz, a shell archive of Drivers/Dp/{fdtestdp.f,RES}, Drivers/Sp/ and Src/src.f
code.note: Unshar the archive (it only creates files; read it first). The driver fdtestdp.f needs the four functions FDM0P5, FDP0P5, FDP1P5, FDP2P5 and CHEVAL from Src/src.f converted to double precision as the comments in the code instruct. Fortran 77: expect gfortran needs -std=legacy.

claim.location: The authors' own test driver Drivers/Dp/fdtestdp.f prints, for each function and 15 arguments per half-range, 'EXACT VALUE', 'COMP. VALUE' and 'REL. ERROR' (shipped as Drivers/Dp/RES). The EXACT VALUE column is a 16-digit table written into the driver's DATA statements (ARMP5M/P, AR0P5M/P, AR1P5M/P, AR2P5M/P), independent of the code under test. Registered: the 8th reference point of each of the 8 arrays, by that fixed rule.
claim.metric: COMP. VALUE printed by the shipped driver for each function and argument, compared with its EXACT VALUE

tolerance.abs: per value, in values[].tol_abs (1e-5 times the exact value)
tolerance.basis: Fixed before any run. The driver prints COMP. VALUE with 7 significant digits, so a printed value can differ from the 16-digit exact value by up to about 5e-6 relative by rounding alone; 1e-5 allows that and nothing more. The shipped RES shows the code's true relative error at about 1e-15, so this tolerance cannot hide a real failure of the algorithm. Not to be loosened after any run.

cost.data_licence: No data. ACM code licence not stated in the archive; the rerun should record it.

why: The authors ship an independent 16-digit table of exact values and their own results; the code (Chebyshev series, 1990s Fortran 77) must compute every value, so this tests whether a 1998 numerical library still builds and still agrees with its published accuracy on a current compiler.
